title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — if the pre-law world-sin is not the act, what is it?
pass_a_gloss: Placeus turns GAR.3 back: Paul speaks of the sin that was in the world until the law—so what is that sin? The act? No: the learned man himself grants the act did not last until the law, since it passed in a moment.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Since, then, the Apostle speaks of the sin which was in the world until the law, what is to be understood by that sin?
The act? By no means: for the learned man confesses that it did not last until the law, since it passed in a moment.
source_text: PLAC. Cum igitur Apostolus loquatur de peccato quod usque ad legem fuit in mundo, quid per illud peccatum intelligendum est? Actus? Minime: fatetur enim Vir doctus illum non durasse usque ad legem, cum momento transierit.

choices.choice: Pre-law world-sin cannot be the momentary act
